inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $46M (ShareBasedCompensation) plus ~$15M estimated cash taxes on net-share settlement (FY2019-21 disclosed run-rate $17-20M; not tagged in XBRL since 2022). PPG publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC figure.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares Q2 2026 10-Q (223.9M; 222.3M basic outstanding at 2026-06-30). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. PPG is an active repurchaser ($790M FY2025, $175M H1 2026), so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~4.9% (after-tax ~3.8%) at ~23% debt / 77% equity on market values -> ~8.2%. Rounded up to 8.5%. Same WACC in every scenario: cyclicality (auto OEM, Europe) is charged in the bear flows, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost ($588M liability at FY2025) is already inside operating expense and therefore inside EBITDA; lease liabilities are EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment (leases as operating cost), consistent.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI earns ~$16M/yr, ~1% of NI); the NCI stock is deducted once in the equity bridge at book value ($147M, 2026-06-30). Not also removed from the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: US operating industrial, moderately cyclical; owner-fcf.md + adaptations for NCI, leases and risk-charged-once). First valuation of this ticker. NET DEBT at 2026-06-30 (Q2 2026 10-Q, filed 2026-07-29): debt $6,886M (current $691M incl. $4M short-term borrowings + long-term $6,195M) less cash $1,520M and short-term investments $74M = $5,292M. INTEREST INCOME not stripped: PPG is net-debt, and the component build is unlevered (EBIT-based), so interest income never enters the projected flows. BASE YEAR NORMALIZATION: FY2025 is used as FY0 because it is clean continuing operations: the FY2024 one-offs ($285M loss on the US/Canada architectural sale, $146M Russia impairment, $233M restructuring) are non-cash or discontinued and do not enter the component build; FY2024 and earlier revenue includes or is restated around divestitures (FY2021 and earlier rows are pre-restatement and still contain US/Canada architectural and silicas). FY2025 reported EBITDA reconstructed from XBRL: pretax $2,045M + interest expense $241M - interest income $153M + depreciation $403M + amortization $125M = $2,661M (16.8% margin, post-SBC). Pre-SBC that is ~17.1%; adding back ~$90M of adjusted-EPS exclusions other than amortization gives ~17.6%. FY2026 base starts at 17.3% because H1 2026 reported EBITDA margin was ~16.7% (vs 17.6% H1 2025) despite +6.9% sales, so the cost program has not yet shown up in reported margins. FY2026 revenue +5.5%: H1 2026 $8,425M (+6.9% incl. ~3pp FX) and H2 assumed +4%. CAPEX was elevated at 4.5-4.9% of revenue in FY2024-25 (aerospace/Asia capacity) vs 2.5-3.2% FY2015-23; H1 2026 capex $309M; path tapers to 3.2% by FY2030. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer with receivables + inventory > payables, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture -12%). CASH TAX 23% of EBIT (FY2025 taxes paid $438M = 21.4% of pretax; provision 22.4%). EQUITY BRIDGE: NCI at book and ~$100M estimated remaining cash cost of the $175M-savings restructuring program. Pension funded status not modelled (no material deficit disclosed in the XBRL feed); flag for a future refresh.

equity_bridge.item: Remaining cash restructuring for the ~$175M cost program
equity_bridge.note: Estimate: FY2024 charge $233M, partly paid through H1 2026

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base driver path FY2027-29 (3.5%); equity CAGR not used because it diverges from revenue
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.85% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 2.79% (3yr 0.55%): >30% divergence. Equity growth reflects retained earnings and FX on a business whose revenue has been flat once divestitures are stripped out; it overstates organic growth.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue: FY2022 onward is restated continuing operations (ex US/Canada architectural, ex silicas); FY2021 and earlier is as originally reported, so the 5-year CAGR mixes bases and the 3-year (0.55%) is the cleaner read. EPS 3-year CAGR (17%) starts from a FY2022 trough ($4.34, raw-material squeeze) and the FY2025 $6.96 includes discontinued items; adjusted EPS fell slightly in FY2025 ($7.58). Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - est. equity-award taxes): FY2020 $1,765M, FY2022 $429M (working-capital build), FY2025 $1,102M; FCF CAGRs swing on working capital and the FY2024-25 capex step-up and are not a usable growth signal. SBC is ~0.3% of revenue and is not growing faster than cash flow.

base.narrative: Guidance-anchored FY2026, then low-single-digit growth and ~120bp of margin recovery from the cost program by FY2029.

bull.narrative: Aerospace and packaging compound, Europe recovers, full cost savings drop through; margin reaches 20%.

bear.narrative: Auto OEM / European industrial downturn in FY2027 with index-contract price resets; savings absorbed by price, margin stuck near 16%.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands inside the reaffirmed $7.70-8.10 adjusted-EPS range on ~5.5% reported sales growth (H1 +6.9%, FX-assisted). From FY2027 PPG grows at its end markets plus a little: aerospace coatings (backlog ~$315M, double-digit organic) and packaging (BPA-NI reformulation) offset flat European auto OEM and architectural, giving ~3-3.5% nominal growth. The ~$175M cost program and the elimination of stranded costs from the US/Canada architectural and silicas exits lift pre-SBC EBITDA margin from ~17.3% to 18.5% by FY2029, roughly half the gross savings retained after price give-backs on index-based industrial contracts. Capex tapers from the FY2024-25 capacity step-up (4.5-4.9% of sales) back toward ~3.2%, which is where most of the cash-flow improvement comes from.
scenario_narratives.bull: The portfolio simplification works as management pitches it: the remaining business is a specialty-coatings mix (aerospace, refinish, packaging, protective) that grows mid-single-digit, Europe recovers from its 2023-26 trough, LatAm architectural keeps growing, and the full cost savings drop through, taking margin to 20% (still below Sherwin-Williams). Buybacks continue at the FY2025 pace. Exit at 17x owner FCF, in line with where coatings peers trade in normal markets.
scenario_narratives.bear: Industrial Coatings takes the hit the analysis flags: an auto-OEM and European industrial downturn in FY2027 flattens sales, and falling raw-material indices reset contract prices downward, so margin drops ~110bp and the cost program only offsets price erosion. PPG, now without the US/Canada architectural repaint base that cushioned past cycles, recovers only to ~16% margin and 2% growth. Not a solvency case: interest cover ~8x and net debt ~2x EBITDA. Exit at 12x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default because Industrial Coatings is genuinely cyclical, European demand is still soft and PPG no longer has the US repaint base to cushion a downturn. Base 50% as the guidance-anchored path. Bull cut to 25% from 35% because it needs three independent things at once (Europe recovery, full savings retention and sustained aerospace/packaging growth), and FY2025 adjusted EPS actually declined, so self-help has not yet shown up in earnings.

valuation_philosophy.summary: PPG is valued as a mature, moderately cyclical specialty-coatings franchise on a strict owner-FCF basis, unlevered, at an 8.5% USD WACC with a 12-17x terminal cap. Value hinges on two levers: whether the cost program lifts margins (~120bp in base) and whether capex normalizes from the FY2024-25 step-up. Divestiture losses and the Russia impairment are non-cash/discontinued and do not enter the flows. SBC is small (~0.4% of revenue incl. withholding), so house and street bases sit close together.
key_risks_to_valuation: Auto OEM and European industrial cyclicality hitting Industrial Coatings volumes and index-linked pricing
Cost-program savings competed away rather than retained in margin
Capex staying near 4.5% of revenue instead of tapering to ~3.2%
FX: a large share of revenue is outside the US, and FX helped FY2025/H1 2026
Terminal cap multiple: the base binds at 15x; each 1x is roughly $5/share
